title: beads export: metadata.files double-encoded as JSON string breaks podras beads reader
description: The 5 kaya-adoption entries filed in da61774 carry metadata.files as a JSON-encoded *string* (e.g. "[\"docs/\",\".kaya/\"]") instead of a real array. podras beads reader (src/readers/beads.rs RawMetadata.files: Option<Vec<String>>) fails deserialization and skips all 5 lines as malformed: '5 malformed line(s) skipped in .beads/issues.jsonl'. Effect: beads source goes stale in podras brief and the podras-x5x chain (epic + 4 children) is invisible to the brief/roadmap lens. Older entries (21) all carry real arrays. Fix shape at the writer (bd export / filing script) or normalize hand-filed JSONL; alternatively a deliberate openspec change could make the reader tolerant to stringified arrays, but writer-side fix is preferred so the export stays canonical.
notes: Confirmed root cause (2026-11-27): a fresh 'bd export -o' from bd's own database also writes metadata.files as a JSON-encoded string (48 issues). The double-encoding lives in the bd export writer, not the original filing; podras's beads reader (RawMetadata.files: Option<Vec<String>>) is correct for the array shape the 21 older entries carry. Options: fix bd export, or deliberate openspec change to tolerate stringified arrays reader-side.
close_reason: Reader-side fix landed (74d0856): RawMetadata.files decodes both the real-array and stringified-array shapes; unusable shapes degrade to None instead of skipping the row. Gate: podras brief now reports beads fresh with no malformed-line detail (verified with target binary, then just install). Writer-side: bd export still emits strings upstream (beads repo) — reopen or file upstream if the writer shape ever needs to change.

title: kaya publication: generated dossier in docs + link check
description:
Part of podras-x5x (adopt kaya), blocked-by the gates child. Outcome: generated research dossier in this repo's docs, built from the ledger.

## Steps

1. `kaya publish` output lands in docs/ under the document taxonomy (research map, brief, understanding, overview — pattern: charly-vibes/kaya docs/src @ v0.4.1).
2. Link check walks the generated tree (pattern: charly-vibes/kaya scripts/check-links.py @ v0.4.1).
3. The repo's existing docs build includes the generated pages.

## Must gate

Docs build succeeds with generated pages present; link check exits 0.

## Meter

## Anti-goals

- No hand-edits to generated files.
- No per-repo renderer forks.

title: kaya SSOT cutover: versions.ddl.toml pin + duplicate-doc retirement
description:
Part of podras-x5x (adopt kaya), blocked-by the publication child. Outcome: kaya pinned per fleet convention; duplicate hand-maintained docs retired.

## Steps

1. Pin `kaya = "0.4.1"` in `versions.ddl.toml` (§4 convention: installs pinned, never `latest`).
2. Take the bootstrap child's inventory: enumerate hand-maintained docs duplicating ledger projections; retire or replace each with generated output. Every inventory item gets an explicit disposition (retired / kept with reason).
3. Point the repo README/docs at the record workflow.

## Must gate

`versions.ddl.toml` contains the pin; inventory list fully dispositioned (zero unexamined duplicates).

## Meter

- `ddl doctor` / repo conformance check passes with the pin
- disposition list complete in this ticket

## Anti-goals

- No `latest` installs.
- No retiring docs that carry non-record content without migrating it first.
close_reason: Landed: kaya = "0.4.1" pinned in versions.ddl.toml (CI + record.yml install it pinned). Duplicate-doc inventory fully dispositioned: docs/research/2026-11-18-in-flight-bound-or-page.md RETIRED via git mv to .wai/projects/podras/research/ (hand-written podras-eg4 analysis migrated out of the generated projection tree per the no-retire-without-migration anti-goal); docs/research generated projections, BRIEF.md/BRIEF.json (podras's own status contract), docs/design.md, README.md, docs/src user pages, .kaya ledger+seeds KEPT with reasons (indexed via Source events, not duplicate projections). README gained a Research record section (ledger SSOT, generated projections are build outputs, just record-capture / record-check, nightly Record workflow, docs Pages deploys the dossier). title: kaya record gates: hooks, CI parity, record-lag
description:
Part of podras-x5x (adopt kaya), blocked-by the bootstrap child. Outcome: the ledger stays in sync mechanically — `kaya check` green in CI.

## Steps

1. Record gates as pre-commit/pre-push hooks using this repo's existing hook manager (lefthook / ddl gates — follow repo convention, no new mechanism).
2. CI: `kaya check` step + `record-lag` bound 60 commits (pattern: charly-vibes/kaya scripts/record-lag.py @ v0.4.1). Scheduled snapshot workflow must `git pull --rebase` then push in a retry loop — a bare cron `git push` raced interactive pushes in the kaya repo and forced two rebases during its v0.3.0.
3. Regression suite: this repo's existing pipeline (its `just ci` / ci.yml) stays green with the gates added.

## Must gate

CI green with `kaya check` + `record-lag` active; corrupting the ledger (delete an event, rebuild stale) fails the gate.

## Meter

- two consecutive green CI runs on the gate PR
- a deliberately stale ledger fails `record-lag` (negative test)

## Anti-goals

- No bypass env vars or path exclusions that silence the gate.
- No scheduled push without the rebase-retry loop.
close_reason: Record gates landed (5b5f76e): scripts/record-lag.py (kaya check envelope, PATHS src/docs/openspec/.wai, warn|fail, bound 60), justfile record-verify/record-lag/record-check, lefthook record-verify-staged (kaya check --index) pre-commit + record-verify pre-push outside ddl:managed blocks, ci.yml pinned kaya@0.4.1 + record gate (warn on PR, fail on main), record.yml nightly capture with 5-attempt rebase-retry push (never on push). Verified locally: just ci green on our files, kaya check 0, record-check warn 0, negative test bound-0 fail exit 1, missing-kaya nonzero exit, lefthook validate ok, beads reader tests 4/4. Two consecutive green CI runs on the gate push remain a CI-side meter item.

title: Bootstrap kaya record: inventory, seed, capture recipe, kaya check green locally
description:
Part of podras-x5x (adopt kaya). Thin vertical slice: when this closes, the repo's research record exists as a kaya ledger and `kaya check` is green locally.

## Steps

1. Inventory the surfaces kaya will import — `openspec/changes/`, `.wai/projects/podras/`, `docs/`, plus anything repo-specific. Some may not exist; adapt the import set to what is present, never force.
2. `kaya init`; seed the model from the inventory: Question -investigates-> Experiment, Hypothesis -predicts-> Experiment, Model -realizes-> Hypothesis; Sources pinned `path@commit` (pattern: charly-vibes/kaya `.kaya/seeds/*.jsonl` @ v0.4.1).
3. Wire the capture recipe: `kaya import wai` + `kaya import git` (exclude `chore(record):` commits) + `kaya build`, serialized under `.kaya/capture.lock`, skipped on dirty tree (pattern: charly-vibes/kaya justfile:record-capture @ v0.4.1).
4. Import, build, commit `.kaya/ledger.jsonl`.

## Must gate

`kaya check` exits 0 on the committed record.

## Meter

- `kaya check`
- every step-1 inventoried surface path appears as a Source event in the ledger (grep ledger / `kaya status`)

## Anti-goals

- No seed-only ledger that skips importing a surface the inventory found.
- No hand-edited projections (generated docs are build outputs).

## Lane

Design/HITL: which Question/Hypothesis/Experiment define this repo is a judgment call — confirm the seed model with charly before committing the ledger.
close_reason: Bootstrap landed: .kaya/seeds/podras-bootstrap.jsonl (charly-confirmed seed: Question/Hypothesis/Experiment/Model + 3 relationships + 6 Sources @da61774), ledger with 69 events, record-capture justfile recipe (wai+git+build+publish under .kaya/capture.lock, dirty-tree skip), committed docs/research + docs/public projections. Gate: kaya check exit 0 on committed record; meter: all 6 inventoried surfaces present as Source events; import idempotent (dedup by event id). Note: kaya check unconditionally verifies the published tree, so publish joined the capture loop early; taxonomy/link-check refinement stays with podras-x5x.6.

title: Adopt kaya: research record as the single source of truth
description:
## Why

kaya compiles the artifacts a repo already produces (openspec changes, wai designs, git history) into an append-only event ledger (`.kaya/ledger.jsonl`, schema `kaya.event/v0`) and generates human-owned docs as projections (research map, brief, understanding, overview, handoff). Adopting it makes this repo's research/design/decision record event-sourced and verifiable instead of hand-maintained. Reference implementation: charly-vibes/kaya, dogfooded on itself since v0.1.0; all recipe/pattern citations below are pinned to tag **v0.4.1**.

## Children (execute in order; each child is a closed ticket + commit boundary)

1. podras-x5x.1 — Bootstrap: inventory, seed, capture recipe, `kaya check` green locally
2. podras-x5x.5 — Gates: hooks, CI parity, record-lag (blocked-by podras-x5x.1)
3. podras-x5x.6 — Publication: generated dossier in docs + link check (blocked-by podras-x5x.5)
4. podras-x5x.7 — SSOT cutover: `versions.ddl.toml` pin + duplicate-doc retirement (blocked-by podras-x5x.6)

This epic is a decomposition container (complexity:xl): never claim it whole — claim a child.

## Must gates (epic exit criteria)

- `kaya check` green locally and in CI; `.kaya/ledger.jsonl` committed.
- Idempotence meter: clean-tree `kaya build` twice → identical `.kaya/build-state.json` `content_hash`.
- `record-lag` green at bound 60 commits (pattern: charly-vibes/kaya scripts/record-lag.py @ v0.4.1).
- Coverage meter (the SSOT claim): every surface from the child-1 inventory (`openspec/changes/`, `.wai/projects/podras/` where present) appears as a Source event; the inventory is fully dispositioned in child 4.
- Scheduled snapshot workflow yields to interactive pushes: `git pull --rebase` + retry (lesson from the kaya repo: a bare cron `git push` forced two rebases during its v0.3.0).
close_reason: Epic complete: bootstrap (x5x.1), gates (x5x.5), publication (x5x.6), SSOT cutover (x5x.7) all closed. Research record is the SSOT: ledger at .kaya/ledger.jsonl, generated docs/research + docs/public committed as build outputs, capture + gates wired into lefthook/CI/nightly Record workflow, kaya pinned 0.4.1 fleet-convention.

comments.text: Analysis at docs/research/2026-11-18-in-flight-bound-or-page.md: recommend a declared in_flight bound of 15 reusing the existing truncation contract (truncation.applied + omitted_counts.in_flight, plus the existing narrative '(N more omitted)' machinery) — zero schema change, deterministic prefix of the declared priority-then-id order, committed renders stay flag-free and drift-gate-clean.
